text:
Predicates:
Fights(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Loses(x, y) ::: x loses to y.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
AppearsIn(x, y) ::: x appears in y.
GoodGuysWin(y) ::: in movie y, good guys always win.
Movie(y) ::: y is a movie.
Character(x) ::: x is a character.
Fights(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Nemesis(x, y) ::: y is the nemesis of x.
Premises:
Movie(theSurprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a movie.
NamedAfter(theSurprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar, SirDigby) ::: The movie is named after Sir Digby.
Character(SirDigby) ::: Sir Digby is a character.
Fights(SirDigby, Nemesis) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
In(movie, y) ::: in movie y, good guys always win.
NamedAfter(x, y) → AppearsIn(y, x) ::: If a movie is named after a character, that character appears in the movie.
Fights(x, y) → Loses(y, x) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting loses.
Movie(y) ∧ NamedAfter(y, x) → AppearsIn(y, x) ::: If a movie is named after a character, that character appears in the movie.
Conclusion:
Loses(Nemesis, SirDigby) ::: Sir Digby’s nemesis loses.
